title: Apply Ohm's law to circuits

hook.scenario: Aapke paas ek 12V ki battery aur ek chhota bulb hai, par aap dar rahe ho ki kahin bulb fuse na ho jaye.
hook.question: Kaise pata chalega ki bulb mein kitna current jayega?

mental_model.intuition: Formula V = IR ek electrical scale ki tarah hai. Koi bhi do values batao, teesri apne aap mil jayegi.
mental_model.description: Agar V = IR hai, toh hum easily I = V/R aur R = V/I nikal sakte hain. Ye triangle (V at top, I and R at bottom) circuit ke kisi bhi component ka behaviour predict karne mein madad karta hai.

explanation:
Circuits solve karte waqt, V = IR sabse important tool hai. Is formula ko 'Ohm's magic triangle' ki madad se bhi yaad rakha jata hai.

Agar humein current nikalna hai, toh I = V / R use karte hain. Isse saaf pata chalta hai ki current resistance ke inversely proportional hai. Agar resistance double ho jaye, toh current aadha (half) ho jayega.

Agar resistance nikalna ho, toh R = V / I use karte hain. Resistance ki unit Ohm hai, jise Greek letter Omega se dikhate hain. 1 Ohm wahi resistance hai jab 1 Volt ki battery 1 Ampere ka current produce kare.

Hamesha yaad rakho, numerical solve karne se pehle values ko standard units (Volt, Ampere, Ohm) mein convert karna zaroori hai. Milliampere (mA) ko 1000 se divide karke Ampere mein convert karna na bhoolein.

worked_example.problem: How much current will an electric bulb draw from a 220 V source, if the resistance of the bulb filament is 1200 ohm?

steps.narration: Question mein di gayi values ko list karte hain.
Ohm's law formula I = V/R use karte hain.

worked_example.problem: The potential difference between the terminals of an electric heater is 60 V when it draws a current of 4 A. What current will the heater draw if the potential difference is increased to 120 V?

steps.narration: Pehle case se heater ka resistance R nikalte hain, jo ki fix rehta hai.
Naye voltage ke saath naya current I nikalne ke liye formula lagate hain.

common_mistakes.title: Forgetting to convert units
common_mistakes.explanation: Using current in milliamperes (mA) directly in the formula V=IR. Always convert mA to A (1 mA = 0.001 A).

recall_questions.q: If voltage is doubled while resistance is kept constant, what happens to the current?

oa_questions.question: Let the resistance of an electrical component remains constant while the potential difference across its ends decreases to half of its former value. What change will occur in the current?
oa_questions.answer: The current will also decrease to half of its former value.
oa_questions.approach: Use the direct proportionality between V and I.
